rfi.title: 'Choose France' summit puts AI at heart of Macron’s €93 billion investment drive
rfi.description: Foreign companies have pledged a total of €93 billion in investment at France's annual Choose France summit, President Emmanuel Macron announced on Monday, with artificial intelligence and data infrastructure projects accounting for the bulk of commitments.

rfi.title: Court rejects Rwanda €115mn claim against Britain over migrant deal
rfi.description: An international court on Monday rejected a claim by Rwanda for Britain to pay more than £100 million (€115million) it said London still owed from a scrapped deal to deport migrants.

rfi.title: Guineans denounce an 'electoral farce' after low turnout in legislative polls
rfi.description: Legislative and municipal elections were held in Guinea on Sunday to complete the process of returning constitutional order to the country after the December 2025 presidential election While this double ballot took place without major incident, voter turnout was low.

rfi.title: Ethiopia goes to the polls with the result widely seen as a foregone conclusion
rfi.description: Ethiopia holds parliamentary and regional elections on Monday that analysts expect Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party to win by a large margin, despite significant unrest across much of the country.

rfi.title: PSG celebrations marred by violence as French authorities report 890 arrests
rfi.description: French authorities have arrested over 890 people after outbreaks of violence followed Paris Saint-Germain’s Champions League victory on Saturday, as the government defended its policing operation amid sharp criticism from the right.

rfi.title: France boards fourth Russian oil tanker as crackdown on ‘shadow fleet’ continues
rfi.description: The French Navy has boarded another oil tanker from Russia as Paris steps up its campaign against Moscow’s so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels suspected of evading international sanctions.

rfi.title: France weighs tougher safeguards against child abuse in schools
rfi.description: French lawmakers will on Monday debate tougher protections against sexual abuse in schools and after-school programmes, as a series of scandals increases pressure on the government to strengthen safeguards.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Bafana Bafana return to the World Cup chasing a first knockout stage
rfi.description: South Africa enter the first 48-team World Cup as Africa's 11th-ranked side in the Fifa standings. In the first instalment of a nine-part series on African squads at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada, RFI looks at a nation making its fourth appearance at the finals.

rfi.title: Last hurrah:  Algeria's Riyad Mahrez
rfi.description: Riyad Mahrez will play for Algeria for the second time at the World Cup at the age of 35. In the fourth instalment of a series on players at their final World Cup, RFI looks at the career of a striker who has risen from modest clubs to international stardom.

rfi.title: First contact: Curaçao’s rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Curaçao will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the first instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the smallest nation to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

rfi.title: Football heroes: PSG victory toasted by thousands of fans in Paris
rfi.description: The French capital held a hero's welcome for Paris Saint-Germain players who won their second consecutive Champions League title with celebrations under heavy security after a night of revelry marred by unrest. The team was received by President Emmanuel Macron ahead of a victory parade which drew thousands of supporters.

rfi.title: France requests emergency UN meeting amid Israeli advance in Lebanon
rfi.description: France has requested an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council after Israeli forces seized the medieval Beaufort castle in Lebanon, the French foreign minister said Sunday.

rfi.title: Ethiopia election overshadowed by war, instability and muted opposition
rfi.description: Ethiopia goes to the polls on Monday in an election which is expected to return Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party to power, but has been marked by instability, restricted voting and questions over whether the vote can challenge the status quo.

rfi.title: Hundreds detained after violent clashes on PSG victory night
rfi.description: More than 700 people on Saturday were detained across France, over 200 in Paris alone, after violent clashes erupted when thousands poured onto the streets after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League final victory against English club Arsenal.

rfi.title: Last hurrah: Brazil's Neymar
rfi.description: Neymar will play for Brazil at the World Cup for the fourth time at the age of 34. In the third of a series on players at their final World Cup, RFI looks back at the career of a striker who holds his country's record for both scoring and assisting goals.

rfi.title: Japan's SoftBank to spend €75bn on AI centres in France
rfi.description: Japanese tech investor SoftBank will spend €75 billion ($87.5 billion) on artificial intelligence infrastructure in France, its founder Masayoshi Son told a French newspaper in an interview published Saturday.

rfi.title: Women gain ground in France as running clubs turn sport into community
rfi.description: Statistics show that most people now taking up running in France are women. In Paris, some run alone and some in running groups – which are booming in the French capital as women turn to them for motivation, safety and a sense of community.

rfi.title: 'We are here to help': WHO chief visits epicentre of Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
rfi.description: UN health chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus on Saturday visited Bunia in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo - where a severe Ebola outbreak has been declared.

lemonde.title: Vladimir Poutine essuie une série de revers qui alimentent le mécontentement en Russie et interrogent sa stratégie
lemonde.description: Alors que le chef du Kremlin vante une victoire à portée de main en Ukraine, Kiev multiplie les attaques de drones à l’intérieur du territoire russe. Ces échecs militaires s’ajoutent aux difficultés économiques.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : les affrontements se poursuivent entre le Hezbollah et Israël malgré les déclarations d’apaisement de Donald Trump
lemonde.description: Le Hezbollah a revendiqué des attaques contre l’armée israélienne dans le sud du Liban, tandis que l’agence officielle libanaise y a signalé des frappes israéliennes sur plusieurs villages. Ces échanges de tirs se produisent alors que le président américain a assuré que le mouvement pro-iranien et l’Etat hébreu allaient cesser les hostilités.

lemonde.title: Violences en milieu scolaire : l’Assemblée nationale adopte à l’unanimité la proposition de loi « post-Bétharram »
lemonde.description: Le texte, rédigé après des mois de travaux et d’auditions, prévoit de renforcer le contrôle des intervenants susceptibles d’être au contact des enfants dans les écoles et le périscolaire. Mais il ne lève pas le secret de la confession pour les ministres du culte.

lemonde.title: Immigration : l’Union européenne se dote d’un régime draconien d’expulsion des étrangers sans papiers
lemonde.description: Outre un renforcement des sanctions contre les déboutés du droit d’asile, les Etats, le Parlement et la Commission autorisent la création de centres de rétention à l’étranger pour y renvoyer les migrants en situation irrégulière.

lemonde.title: Agriculture : le projet de loi d’urgence ressort encore plus clivant de son passage à l’Assemblée
lemonde.description: Les députés ont conforté la volonté du gouvernement de faciliter le stockage de l’eau ou l’agrandissement des élevages. Ils sont également allés plus loin que le texte initial concernant la lutte contre la prédation du loup, la concurrence déloyale ou la fixation des prix des matières premières agricoles.

lemonde.title: Areski Belkacem, artiste au talent multiforme et complice indissociable de Brigitte Fontaine, est mort à 86 ans
lemonde.description: Artisan avec Brigitte Fontaine d’une œuvre mêlant poésie, jazz et musiques du monde, Areski Belkacem, plus connu par son simple prénom, est mort lundi, à 86 ans.

lemonde.title: Les primaires en Californie, un test pour les démocrates et un parti divisé
lemonde.description: A la veille du vote du mardi 2 juin, dans un Etat acquis aux démocrates, le débat va se focaliser sur les divisions entre modérés et radicaux, et alimenter celui de la taxation des milliardaires.

lemonde.title: Les premiers résultats de Parcoursup attendus dans la soirée de mardi pour plus d’un million d’étudiants
lemonde.description: Parmi les candidats, figurent 657 000 lycéens scolarisés en France ainsi que 206 000 étudiants souhaitant changer de voie. Le verdict tombera à partir de 19 heures, mais le processus reste conditionné à l’obtention du bac dont les résultats seront communiqués le 7 juillet.

lemonde.title: Après les violences qui ont suivi la victoire du PSG, des peines de prison prononcées : « Sommes-nous une société du chaos ? Non »
lemonde.description: A la suite des 890 interpellations dans plusieurs villes de France, de premières comparutions immédiates ont eu lieu lundi. A Paris, des sanctions sont tombées pour rébellion et violence sur policier, transport et détention d’arme (des mortiers) ou encore pour vol avec violence.

lemonde.title: Disparition de Lyhanna dans le Gers : un homme mis en examen pour enlèvement et séquestration
lemonde.description: Les recherches menées par les gendarmes dans les environs de Fleurance, dans le Gers, n’ont pas permis de retrouver la collégienne de 11 ans qui a été aperçue pour la dernière fois devant son collège, vendredi après-midi, dans le véhicule du suspect. Ce dernier est une connaissance de la famille de Lyhanna.

lemonde.title: Bordeaux refuse de recevoir le « petit musée africain » qu’une sage-femme souhaitait léguer à la ville
lemonde.description: Le conseil municipal a voté à l’unanimité pour le rejet du legs de la collectionneuse, lundi 1ᵉʳ juin, afin de permettre à 53 objets, majoritairement gabonais, de retourner dans leurs pays d’origine.

lemonde.title: « Les journalistes ne seront plus autorisés à pénétrer » : le Pentagone restreint encore l’accès de la presse
lemonde.description: Le Pentagone interdit aux journalistes l’accès à son service de presse, désormais classé zone protégée par le secret défense. La décision s’appuie sur la présence de personnel travaillant sur des documents classifiés.

lemonde.title: Alphabet, la maison mère de Google, veut lever 80 milliards de dollars pour financer son IA

lemonde.title: Comptes de campagne de Jean-Luc Mélenchon en 2017 : l’information judiciaire se clôt sur quatre mises en examen

france24fr.title: Les astronautes français Thomas Pesquet et Arnaud Prost partiront dans l'espace en 2027
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron a annoncé lundi que deux astronautes français partiront dans l'espace en 2027 dans le cadre d'un accord signé avec l'entreprise américaine Vast. Le célèbre Thomas Pesquet partira en tant que commandant de vol pour l'ISS où il a déjà séjourné deux fois, tandis qu'Arnaud Prost se rendra dans station spatiale commerciale Haven-1.

france24fr.title: Forteresse de Beaufort : l'histoire va-t-elle bégayer au Liban ?
france24fr.description: Cela fait plus de 900 ans que la forteresse de Beaufort est disputée. Mais, depuis les années 1970, elle est l'un des symboles des tensions entre Israël et ses ennemis, d'abord l'OLP puis le Hezbollah. Depuis samedi, l'État hébreu a repris le contrôle de ce point stratégique ravivant le sentiment pour tous les Libanais d'une histoire qui ne cesse de se répéter, celle de l'occupation.

france24fr.title: "Fonds anti-instrumentalisation" gelé par la justice : l'administration Trump prend acte
france24fr.description: De nombreux médias américains rapportent lundi que Donald Trump est sur le point de renoncer à son très polémique "fonds anti-instrumentalisation" après le gel provisoire de ce dernier par une juge. Pour l'instant, l'administration Trump, dans un communiqué publié lundi, exprime son "profond désaccord" avec la décision de justice, mais assure qu'il la "respectera".

france24fr.title: Au Danemark, la Première ministre sortante Mette Frederiksen a constitué un gouvernement
france24fr.description: Mette Frederiksen va présenter cette semaine sa nouvelle équipe, après avoir annoncé lundi soir avoir réussi à constituer une coalition gouvernementale de gauche. La Première ministre danoise était sortie affaiblie des élections législatives du 24 mars, puisque le parti social-démocrate qu'elle dirige avait réalisé son plus mauvais résultat depuis 1903.

france24fr.title: Une attaque du groupe jihadiste ADF tue 16 personnes à Beni dans l'est de la RD Congo
france24fr.description: Dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo, les jihadistes ADF, affilié à l’État islamique, ont mené une attaque dans la ville de Beni. C’est la première fois depuis plus de trois ans que les ADF frappent à l’intérieur de la ville, un signe préoccupant.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : Ousmane Sonko annonce que le Pastef ne participera pas au nouveau gouvernement
Au Sénégal, le président nomme un gouvernement boycotté par Ousmane Sonko
france24fr.description: Le nouveau gouvernement sénégalais, dévoilé lundi, contient bien certains membres et alliés du Pastef, le parti d'Ousmane Sonko, malgré le boycott annoncé dans la soirée par ce dernier en raison d'un "désaccord" avec le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye autour de la constitution de la liste.

france24fr.title: Iran : le président Massoud Pezeshkian sur le départ ?
france24fr.description: Alors qu’un accord de cessez-le-feu semble s’éloigner de plus en plus entre l’Iran et les Etats-Unis, des rumeurs ont circulé quant à une démission du président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian.

france24fr.title: Roland-Garros : fin du rêve pour Parry, Auger-Aliassime pour la première fois en quarts
france24fr.description: Les affiches des quarts de finale de Roland-Garros sont quasiment bouclées et elles ne compteront aucun Français : dernière survivante d'une semaine caniculaire, Diane Parry s'est arrêtée lundi. Le Canadien Félix-Auger Aliassime, lui, en revanche, peut continuer de rêver.

france24fr.title: Un hommage national sera rendu à Edgar Morin mercredi aux Invalides
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron présidera, mercredi aux Invalides, un hommage national au sociologue et philosophe Edgar Morin, décédé le 29 mai à l'âge de 104 ans.

france24fr.title: France: l'atout nucléaire pour attirer les data centers
france24fr.description: Au sommet Choose France, des investissements records ont été annoncés et notamment dans la construction de data centers. La France attire ce secteur très énergivore grâce à ses capacités de production d'électricité basées sur le nucléaire. Pour l'instant, elle produit beaucoup plus d'électricité qu'elle n'en consomme mais certains craignent que l'appétit de l'IA force la France à faire des choix au détriment de sa transition énergétique.

france24fr.title: Israël/Liban : un tournant dans le sud ?
france24fr.description: L'armée israélienne a appelé les habitants de la banlieue sud de Beyrouth à évacuer les lieux en prévision de frappes contre le Hezbollah. Cet ordre intervient après une intensification des hostilités dans le sud du Liban au cours du week-end, marquée par la prise de la forteresse médiévale stratégique de Beaufort par les troupes israéliennes. L'ONU s'est dite "très inquiète" et a appelé, ce lundi, toutes les parties à respecter le cessez-le-feu et à éviter une "nouvelle escalade".

france24fr.title: En direct : Trump affirme qu'Israël a accepté de ne pas envoyer de troupes à Beyrouth
Madagascar : quatre juges de la Haute Cour constitutionnelle dans le viseur de la justice
france24fr.description: À Madagascar, des magistrats se retrouvent dans le viseur de la justice. Le parquet d'Antananarivo souhaite engager des poursuites contre quatre juges de la Haute Cour constitutionnelle accusés de complot en vue de déstabilisation. Une procédure qui intervient après que cette même cour a jugé irrecevable une requête en destitution du président malgache.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi la propagandiste russe Xenia Fedorova embarrasse-t-elle l’exécutif français ?
france24fr.description: Chroniqueuse dans les médias de la galaxie Bolloré au service de la propagande russe, Xenia Fedorova embarrasse désormais l’exécutif à double titre : le ministre de l’Intérieur a dû expliquer pourquoi son titre de séjour avait été renouvelé pour dix ans en 2024, tandis que la ministre de l’Agriculture a participé à un déjeuner en sa compagnie.

france24fr.title: La France et la Russie à couteaux tirés ?
france24fr.description: La marine de Brest a arraisonné hier le "Tagor", un pétrolier sous sanctions européennes en provenance de Russie. Il s'agit du quatrième pétrolier de la flotte fantôme, utilisée par Moscou pour contourner les sanctions, à être intercepté par la France depuis septembre. Les explications avec Nicolas Tenzer, politologue, enseignant à Sciences Po, spécialiste des questions stratégiques et internationales.

zeit.description: In Kyjiw und Dnipro sind in der Nacht mindestens fünf Menschen durch russische Angriffe getötet worden. Es gibt viele Verletzte. In Kyjiw stürzte ein Wohngebäude ein.

zeit.description: In Mexiko haben Lehrkräfte kurz vor der Fußball-WM für mehr Lohn demonstriert. Die Polizei setzte Tränengas ein, als sie auf die geplante Fanmeile vordringen wollten.

zeit.title: Prokrastination: Hausaufgaben? Mach ich später...
zeit.description: Prokrastination fühlt sich nie gut an. Der Psychologe Herbert Scheithauer erklärt, warum Eltern ihren Kindern früh helfen sollten, das ständige Aufschieben zu überwinden.

zeit.title: Zulagen im öffentlichen Dienst: Schafft die Zulagen für Beamte ab
zeit.description: 2.200 Euro im Monat für die Kinder, 600 Euro für den Wohnort: Die Zulagen von Beamten sind teilweise absurd hoch und undurchsichtig. Und unfair gegenüber Angestellten.

zeit.title: Rentenreform: Bärbel Bas will Beamte in gesetzliche Rentenversicherung einbeziehen
zeit.description: Bereits bei der jetzigen Reform sollte Bas zufolge ein gemeinsames System das Ziel sein. Im Gegenzug kann sie sich in Zukunft einen späteren Renteneintritt vorstellen.

letemps.description:

nzz.title: «Der Präsident ist ein sehr kranker Mann»: Nicht erst seit Donald Trump wird über jedes Hämatom im Oval Office spekuliert
nzz.description: Der mächtigste Mann der Welt kann sich keine Schwäche leisten. So soll Joe Bidens geistiger Abbau viele Jahre verschleiert worden sein. Doch schon früher kam es zu abenteuerlichen Vertuschungen gesundheitlicher Probleme im Weissen Haus.

nzz.title: Historischer Prozess gegen Asad-Schergen: Syrischer Geheimdienstchef muss sich in Wien wegen Folter verantworten

nzz.description: Schon wieder verwandelt sich Paris nach einem Fussballspiel in ein Schlachtfeld. Staat und Politik wirken überfordert. Das bestätigt eine unheilvolle Diagnose des französischen Präsidenten.

nzz.description: Islamisten morden nicht aus sozialer Frustration, sondern aus dem Bewusstsein theologischer Überlegenheit. Doch Europa will dies nicht wahrhaben und bekämpft den Terror hartnäckig mit Sozialarbeit und «interreligiösem Dialog».

nzz.description: Auf dem Papier glänzt der Münchner mit 805 Kilometern Reichweite und einem radikal neuen Cockpit. Doch in der Praxis offenbart er noch gewisse Schwächen.

nzz.title: Heute Longines, morgen Jaeger-LeCoultre: Prominente werben schamlos für alles Mögliche. Was bringt das den Unternehmen?

nzz.title: FMH-Präsidentin Gilli: «Wenn sich die Stimmung weiter in Richtung nationaler Abschottung bewegt, wird es für uns brandgefährlich»
nzz.description: Die Schweiz habe die Ausbildung in der Medizin über Jahrzehnte vernachlässigt, sagt Yvonne Gilli, die Präsidentin des Schweizer Ärzteverbands. Sie warnt vor einem Systemkollaps – unabhängig davon, wie die Abstimmung zur 10-Millionen-Initiative ausgeht.

nzz.title: Die Ukraine setzt jetzt auf Roboter
nzz.description: Bodenroboter galten lange Zeit als teure Spielerei. Mittlerweile nutzt die Ukraine Tausende von ihnen, um Soldaten aus der Todeszone an der Front zu holen. Das ist die nächste Stufe der Automatisierung des Krieges.

nzz.title: In der südspanischen Provinz Almería züchten Tausende von Bauern unser Gemüse – zum Teil unter prekären Bedingungen
nzz.description: Über ein Drittel des Gemüses, das in der EU und in der Schweiz verzehrt wird, stammt aus südspanischen Gewächshäusern. Die Produzenten sind meist kleine Familienbetriebe. Wegen des starken Preisdrucks zahlen manche ihren Arbeitern Dumpinglöhne.

nzz.title: Ist die Zuwanderung schuld an der Wohnungsnot? Eine Beweisaufnahme
nzz.description: Die SVP macht die hohen Mieten zu einem Argument für ihre 10-Millionen-Initiative. Die Anklage gegen die Zuwanderung ist nicht aus der Luft gegriffen – doch es gibt mehrere Mittäter.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Eine normale Katholikin wird nicht mit 14 Jahren unglücklich»: Eine Aussteigerin erzählt vom Leben im sagenumwobenen Opus Dei
nzz.description: Das Opus Dei galt als Liebling des Vatikans, Kritiker nennen es eine Sekte. Jüngst prüfte Papst Franziskus schwere Vorwürfe gegen das «Werk Gottes». Nun berichtet Marina Pereda von einem Leben zwischen Putzdienst und Selbstkasteiung – und davon, wie man den Weg hinaus findet.

observador.title: Festival ao Largo muda-se para Belém em julho
observador.description: De 3 a 25 de julho, o festival gratuito do Opart leva música clássica e bailado à Praça Central do CCB, enquanto o São Carlos está em obras financiadas pelo PRR.

observador.title: Nairobi. Centenas protestam contra assassínios de crianças
observador.description: Manifestantes paralisaram Nairobi com cânticos e gritos de dor, bloqueando uma avenida com painel que exibia os nomes de vítimas. Desde janeiro, 69 mulheres morreram e 10.581 crianças desapareceram.

observador.title: Detido suspeito de agredir companheira em Serpa
observador.description: O suspeito terá agredido fisicamente a companheira, no decorrer de uma discussão no interior da casa, provocando-lhe lesões visíveis na face. Um dos filhos menores terá presenciado a situação.

observador.title: Cortes internacionais deixam 130.000 crianças à fome
observador.description: PAM alerta que os cortes, incluindo dos EUA, reduzem refeições escolares e suspendem apoio nutricional a 56.000 bebés. 73% da população poderá ficar sem nutrientes essenciais.

observador.title: Centro Náutico de Montemor-o-Velho recuperado para Europeu
observador.description: A infraestrutura municipal de desportos náuticos teve danos estruturais relevantes na torre de chegada e em equipamentos diversos que comprometeram, de forma significativa, o seu funcionamento.

observador.title: Detido suspeito de fogo florestal em Amarante
observador.description: O suspeito terá provocado o incêndio com recurso a chama direta, aparentemente na sequência de desentendimentos com vizinhos, criando perigo para uma área florestal significativa em Amarante.

observador.title: Cavaco avisa Montenegro para não ceder na reforma do Estado
observador.description: Ex-Presidente ataca "burocratas" que tentam travar Reforma do Estado e dá força a Matias. Ataca Tribunal de Contas e pede a Montenegro "inteligência" e "discernimento" para apostar nesta reforma.

observador.title: A reforma do Estado e o poder dos burocratas
observador.description: Se as reações dos serviços públicos são compreensíveis, o mesmo não se pode dizer do Tribunal de Contas que perante a proposta da sua reforma se assumiu como se fosse um detentor de poder burocrático.

observador.title: Lítio. Empresa garante atuar em Boticas cumprindo a lei
observador.description: A Savannah informou que não tinha sido notificada de qualquer providência cautelar pelo Tribunal Administrativo e Fiscal de Mirandela, continuando os trabalhos a decorrer.

observador.title: Califórnia reconhece Dia dos Açores e Dia de Portugal
observador.description: Para comemorar o reconhecimento dos dias com 51 votos a favor, a republicana Alexandra Macedo ofereceu aos representantes massa sovada de uma padaria portuguesa, situada no seu distrito.

observador.title: Chega quer mais autonomia nas Escolas Profissionais
observador.description: Para o Chega nos Açores, o ensino profissional tem competências e deve ter condições para decidir, propor e executar formação com verdadeiro impacto na empregabilidade dos jovens.

observador.title: Sérgio Conceição vê oficializada saída do Al-Ittihad
observador.description: A decisão surgiu na sequência de uma análise e avaliação exaustivas do desempenho da equipa ao longo do período recente, em consonância com os objetivos e aspirações do clube para a próxima fase.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Fernverkehrszüge waren im Mai wieder unpünktlicher
spiegel.description: Wer in einen Fernzug der Deutschen Bahn steigt, kommt weiter nur in sechs von zehn Fällen planmäßig an. Im Mai hat die Pünktlichkeit lediglich knapp eine wichtige Zielmarke erreicht.

spiegel.title: Todd Blanche und Donald Trump: Der Racheengel des Präsidenten
spiegel.description: Er galt als einer der Fairsten seines Fachs, nun ist Todd Blanche Trumps Mann fürs Schmutzige: Er genehmigt brutale Hinrichtungsmethoden und nutzt sein neues Amt aus, um Widersacher des Präsidenten zu verfolgen.

spiegel.title: ZDF-Doku »Generation Porno«: Merlin war 12, als er 20 Stunden Porno am Stück guckte
Marathon-Paar Esther und Hendrik Pfeiffer: Kann Liebe im Sport besser und schneller machen?
spiegel.description: Kann Liebe im Sport besser und schneller machen? Im Interview erzählen Esther und Hendrik Pfeiffer, wie ihre Ehe sie zu neuen Bestleistungen treibt und was Hobbysportler für ihre Beziehung mitnehmen können.

spiegel.title: Fitness: Sie haben Arthrose im Knie? Darum ist Sport die beste Lösung
spiegel.description: Rund sechs Millionen Menschen in Deutschland leiden an Arthrose im Knie. Wegen der Schmerzen bewegen viele sich kaum noch. Schonung ist genau falsch, sagen Experten.

spiegel.title: News: Péter Magyar, Friedrich Merz, Donald Trump, Benjamin Netanyahu, Libanon, Dario Amodei, Anthropic
spiegel.description: Der ungarische Premier Péter Magyar besucht Friedrich Merz. Donald Trump versucht, die Irangespräche am Laufen zu halten. Anthropic plant einen der größten Börsengänge der Geschichte. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Florida verklagt ChatGPT-Entwickler OpenAI
spiegel.description: Floridas Generalstaatsanwalt erhebt schwere Vorwürfe gegen das Unternehmen OpenAI. Der KI-Assistent ChatGPT sei insbesondere für Teenager problematisch und bedrohe die öffentliche Sicherheit.

spiegel.title: Russland greift Kyjiw mit Raketen und Drohnen an – Wohnblock stürzt ein
spiegel.description: In der Nacht hat es schwere russische Luftangriffe auf Kyjiw gegeben. Menschen flüchteten sich in U-Bahn-Stationen und Luftschutzkeller. Laut Bürgermeister Klitschko wurde ein großes Wohnhaus zerstört, unter den Trümmern werden Opfer befürchtet.

spiegel.title: USA dürften trans Menschen nicht aus den Streitkräften verbannen
spiegel.description: Donald Trump will keine trans Personen in den Reihen des US-Militärs dulden. Doch vor Gericht scheiterte sein Vorstoß nun erneut. Ausgefochten ist der Fall damit aber noch lange nicht.

spiegel.title: Bärbel Bas (SPD) über Hass-Nachrichten: »Bin ein personifiziertes Feindbild geworden«
spiegel.description: Ihr schlage purer Hass entgegen: Sozialministerin Bärbel Bas hat über den Umgang mit persönlichen Angriffen gesprochen. »Je härter und stärker das wird, umso mehr denkt man darüber nach, wie lange hält man das aus?«

spiegel.title: Donald Trump zieht offenbar Plan für umstrittenen Entschädigungsfonds zurück
spiegel.description: Das ging sogar vielen Trump-Jüngern zu weit: Der US-Präsident wollte aus einem Milliardentopf unter anderem Angreifer vom 6. Januar 2021 entschädigen. Nach reichlich Widerstand ist der Plan offenbar vorerst vom Tisch.

spiegel.title: Dänermark: Mette Frederiksen gelingt Regierungsbildung nach Hängepartie
spiegel.description: Mette Frederiksen hat sich ihre dritte Amtszeit als dänische Regierungschefin gesichert. Fast zehn Wochen nach der Parlamentswahl verkündete sie die Einigung auf eine Koalition aus vier Parteien.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Beschwerden von Soldaten - »Angst kann man nicht mit Angst besiegen«
spiegel.description: Monatelange Fronteinsätze ohne Ablösung, Konflikte mit Kommandeuren: Ukrainische Soldaten kämpfen mit Entbehrungen. Olha Reschetylowa soll ihre Rechte stärken. Welche Beschwerden hört sie am häufigsten?

spiegel.title: Migration und Asyl: Europäische Union macht Weg für Abschiebezentren in Drittstaaten frei
spiegel.description: Unterhändler des Europaparlaments und der EU-Länder haben sich auf neue Abschieberegeln verständigt. Diese sehen neben der Erlaubnis von Abschiebezentren in Drittstaaten weitere Verschärfungen vor.

spiegel.title: Belgien: Belgische Fahnder entdecken neue Fährte nach Juwelendiebstahl im Louvre
spiegel.description: In Belgien haben Ermittler auf Handys verdächtige Fotos aus dem Saal im Louvre gefunden, in dem sich die gestohlenen Kronjuwelen befanden. Nun soll geprüft werden, ob es eine Verbindung zu den vier inhaftierten Tatverdächtigen gibt.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: Donald Trump spricht von Fortsetzung der Iran-Gespräche – und Deeskalation zwischen Israel und Hisbollah
spiegel.description: Donald Trump widerspricht Berichten, Iran würde die Verhandlungen mit den USA abbrechen. Zudem habe Israels Premier Netanyahu dem US-Präsidenten in einem Telefonat zugesichert, keine Truppen nach Beirut zu schicken.

spiegel.title: Kevin Keegan: Krebserkrankung von Englands Fußball-Ikone im fortgeschrittenen Stadium
spiegel.description: Nach einem Autounfall entdeckten Ärzte bei Kevin Keegan Krebs: Davon berichtet der frühere englische Nationalcoach und HSV-Star nun. Inzwischen sei die Erkrankung im fortgeschrittenen Stadium.

spiegel.title: Harvard-Universität: Kam ein Nazi in die USA. Und wurde in Ehren empfangen
spiegel.description: Die Harvard-Universität gilt als Eldorado der Wissenschaftsfreiheit. Die ganze Wahrheit ist das nicht. Denn immer wieder beugte sich die Institution den Mächtigen.

elpais.title: Sánchez cuestiona ante su cúpula el trato de la justicia al PSOE
elpais.description: La portavoz de la dirección socialista subraya que la UCO ya ha hecho dos informes sobre Begoña Gómez y todavía ninguno del novio de Ayuso

elpais.title: Jonathan Andic da la batalla de la opinión pública con la vista puesta ya en el jurado popular
elpais.description: El primogénito de Isak Andic, investigado por el presunto homicidio de su padre, fía la misión de revertir el relato a un investigador privado de la defensa

elpais.title: Los datos de precios y compras de vivienda reflejan un mercado al límite en el arranque del año
elpais.description: Los expertos apuntan a las primeras señales de un cambio de signo, aunque solo vaticinan un giro brusco si se agravan los conflictos bélicos

elpais.description: España se enfrenta al reto de acoger a millones de visitantes el 12 de agosto. Ayuntamientos y autonomías ya han elegido 190 miradores para gestionar concentraciones multitudinarias para contemplar el histórico fenómeno

elpais.title: Presunta imparcialidad
elpais.description: El doble rasero judicial y policial acaba erosionando la legitimidad de un poder fundamental del Estado

elpais.description: Esta no es la primera crisis política, pero sí quizás la primera vez en que las redes sociales, liberadas de moderación, actúan como esteroides

elpais.title: El Gobierno suspende el contrato de ciberseguridad del Estado por falta de fondos
elpais.description: El Ministerio para la Transformación Digital paraliza la adjudicación que ganó Telefónica tras un accidentado proceso de licitación con tres cambios de compañía

elpais.title: Las banderas ultras de Abelardo de la Espriella
elpais.description: El vencedor de la primera vuelta, que ha empleado un tono misógino y homofóbico, es admirador de Milei y Bukele, promete recortar 40% de la burocracia del Estado y quiere volver a debatir derechos que ya han ganado las mujeres y la población LGBTI frente al aborto y la adopción de niños

elpais.description: El candidato ultra logra el 43,7 % de los votos frente al 40,9 % de Iván Cepeda, el aspirante de izquierda, en la primera vuelta

elpais.title: Trump intenta rescatar el preacuerdo con Irán y asegura que Israel frenará su ofensiva en Líbano
elpais.description: Netanyahu subraya que su ejército “seguirá actuando en el sur de Líbano como estaba planeado” y atacará también Beirut si Hezbolá sigue disparando contra las localidades del norte de Israel

elpais.title: Etgar Keret, escritor: “Si la vida es una película, Israel es hoy una de zombis”
elpais.description: El narrador mira a la cotidianidad con humor negro y surrealismo en la colección de relatos ‘El blues del fin del mundo’. El ataque de Hamás en 2023 retrasó su publicación

elpais.title: El miedo se apodera de la frontera entre Rumania y Ucrania: “Tenemos la sensación de que algo mucho peor sucederá”
elpais.description: El impacto de un dron en Galati, que causó dos heridos, ha desatado las alarmas entre los vecinos, que temen una escalada por parte de Rusia

elpais.title: La UE reafirma el endurecimiento de su política migratoria al validar la creación de centros de deportación en terceros países
elpais.description: El Consejo y el Parlamento Europeo acuerdan los términos del nuevo reglamento de retornos que allana el camino para enviar a los migrantes rechazados a terceros países fuera de la UE, incluidas familias con menores

elpais.title: Obstáculos en el consulado español de La Habana dificultan los trámites para la regularización de migrantes
elpais.description: Los cubanos denuncian el atasco en la legación para obtener los antecedentes penales, chanchullos para sacar citas y problemas por los apagones eléctricos

elpais.description: Las declaraciones de los primeros acusados evidencian las diferencias en las líneas de defensa de la cúpula política y policial

elpais.title: La Audiencia Nacional obliga al juez Pedraz a reabrir la causa contra el venezolano dueño de las gafas Hawkers
elpais.description: El instructor había archivado la investigación por blanqueo de capitales y la Fiscalía Anticorrupción había presentado un recurso

nyt.title: Trump Backs Off Plan for $1.8 Billion Fund That Drew Political Backlash
nyt.description: The fund has drawn backlash from critics who said it was a scheme to reward President Trump’s political allies with public benefits.

nyt.title: Losing Trust in Justice Dept., Judges Call Out Its Lawyers’ Behavior
nyt.description: The federal courts have long assumed that the government’s lawyers are trustworthy. Now judges across the country are criticizing their lack of candor.

nyt.title: Trump Finds High-Wire Iran Negotiations ‘Very Boring’
nyt.description: President Trump told CNBC that he “couldn’t care less” if the negotiations with Iran break down.

nyt.title: Security Council Members Call for Israel to Withdraw From Southern Lebanon
nyt.description: The U.N. panel met after Israel had threatened to attack southern Beirut. President Trump said later that Israel and Hezbollah had agreed not to attack each other.

nyt.title: U.S. Says More People May Be Charged in Terror Case Linked to Iran
nyt.description: A militia leader pleaded not guilty on Monday to what prosecutors say is his role in attacks that are part of Iran’s response to the war with Israel and the United States.

nyt.title: Anthropic Files to Go Public, Setting Stage for Huge I.P.O.
nyt.description: The artificial intelligence company, which is racing OpenAI to the stock market, has seen explosive growth over the last year thanks largely to technology that can automatically write computer code.

nyt.title: California’s Public Universities Went All in on A.I. Now They’re Tearing Themselves Apart.
nyt.description: California’s public universities spent $16.9 million on A.I. during a financial crisis, and the result has been chaos.

nyt.title: Scott Pelley Accuses CBS News Boss of ‘Murdering’ ‘60 Minutes’
nyt.description: In an explosive staff meeting, Mr. Pelley, a correspondent for the long-running Sunday news show, blasted Bari Weiss, the CBS editor in chief, and Nick Bilton, the show’s new executive producer.

nyt.title: The Return of Blaming and Shaming in Public Health
nyt.description: For years, medicine has tried to eliminate stigma. Now, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is bringing back the language of personal responsibility.

nyt.title: Minnesota Republicans Hold Moment of Silence for Derek Chauvin
nyt.description: Delegates to the Minnesota Republican Party’s convention voted to hold a moment of silence for Derek Chauvin, who was convicted of murdering George Floyd.

nyt.title: Obesity May Be More Prevalent Than Previously Thought
nyt.description: A new study suggests using body mass index alone may miss many people with the disease, but the findings come with caveats.

nyt.title: Mills Reminds Maine Voters She’s ‘Still on the Ballot’ for Senate Amid Platner Controversy
nyt.description: A month after withdrawing from the state’s Senate race, Gov. Janet Mills suggested she remained an option after the likely Democratic nominee, Graham Platner, faced a new scandal.

nyt.title: Previewing California’s Primary Elections and High-Stakes Governor’s Race
nyt.description: The deep-blue state’s primary elections will show how angry voters are at the status quo.

nyt.title: As Ebola Spreads, Scientists Race to Find Vaccines and Treatments
nyt.description: The Bundibugyo virus, a little known type, previously had caused just two small outbreaks. Now it’s at the center of a rapidly widening epidemic in Africa.

nyt.title: What to Know About the Ebola Outbreak
nyt.description: Aid agencies are racing to help health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The virus is known to have killed at least 43, but the true toll may be far higher.

nyt.title: The New Zealand Parakeet Pair That Are Saving Their Species
nyt.description: There are about 450 orange-fronted parakeets left in the world. Super breeders Nacho and Trixie are doing their best to bolster the population.

nyt.title: Marilyn Monroe Fans Descended on Palm Springs For Her 100th Birthday
nyt.description: To honor her centennial, over 1,000 Marilyn Monroe fans came together to dress as the screen legend in Palm Springs, where her Hollywood career began.

nyt.title: Why This Summer Travel Season Will Be a Nightmare
nyt.description: Air travel could be disrupted into next year because of high jet fuel prices.

npr.title: Iran halts talks with U.S. over Israeli actions in Lebanon, Gaza
npr.description: Trumps says Israel and Hezbollah will stop fighting after Iran stops talks with U.S. over Israeli operations in southern Lebanon, Gaza

npr.title: U.S. strikes Iranian military sites. And, Trump's $1.8 billion fund faces scrutiny
npr.description: American aircraft fired on a number of Iranian sites over the weekend, including Qeeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. And, Trump's anti-weaponization fund faces scrutiny in Congress and the courts.

npr.title: Confirmed Ebola cases in Congo near 300 as survivors describe their recoveries
npr.description: The outbreak remains focused in Congo's eastern Ituri province. Congo has reported over 1,000 suspected cases with the Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved treatment or vaccine.

npr.title: Funds for Trump's Board of Peace aren't in World Bank account. So where are they?
npr.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Financial Times reporter Abigail Hauslohner about the funding of President Trump's Board of Peace to oversee Gaza's reconstruction.

npr.title: After Russian missile strike, owners of Ukrainian coffee shop pledge to rebuild
npr.description: After a large-scale Russian missile strike hit downtown Kyiv, the owners of a coffee shop that opened just hours earlier were already serving coffee again and planning to rebuild.

npr.title: Violent clashes give way to peaceful PSG parade after Champions League win
npr.description: A huge crowd of supporters gathered peacefully near the Eiffel Tower on Sunday to celebrate Paris Saint-Germain's victory, which was marred by violent clashes overnight that led police to detain hundreds of people.

npr.title: Right-wing candidate pulls ahead in first round of Colombia's presidential vote
npr.description: Tough-on-crime outsider Aberaldo de la Espriella took the lead in Colombia's presidential race on Sunday night, setting up a runoff with Iván Cepeda, an ally of outgoing President Gustavo Petro.

npr.title: U.S. bombs Iranian military sites, then downs missiles Tehran fired at troops in Kuwait
npr.description: The U.S. says it has bombed radar and drone sites in Iran after Tehran shot down an American drone over the weekend. Iran then said it targeted American soldiers in Kuwait with missiles, which the U.S. says it shot down on Monday.

npr.title: How aid cuts are hampering the front-line response to the Ebola crisis
npr.description: Aid workers in Uganda are watching an Ebola crisis unfold in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. They're doing what they can to prepare for an uptick in cases, but foreign aid cuts aren't helping.

npr.title: The terrifying day the U.S.-Iran war reached a sleepy Sri Lankan town
npr.description: A deadly strike during the first days of the Iran war hit far away in the Indian Ocean, jolting a quiet seaside town and showing how far the conflict's reach extends.

Please state the location and include REMOTE for remote work, REMOTE (US) or similar if the country is restricted, and ONSITE when remote work is not an option.

Please only post if you personally are part of the hiring company—no recruiting firms or job boards. One post per company. If it isn't a household name, explain what your company does.

Please only post if you are actively filling a position and are committed to replying to applicants.

Commenters: please don't reply to job

phys-org.title: Biodiversity offsetting shows promise in pollinator conservation
phys-org.description: Newly created grassland habitats that compensate for nature lost to development can effectively support wild pollinators like bees and hoverflies, according to a first of its kind study in the Netherlands. The findings are published in the Journal of Applied Ecology.

phys-org.title: Making climate-neutral plastics and cosmetics using bacteria
phys-org.description: Plastics, medicines, cosmetics—there are very few everyday products that do not rely on using fossil resources. A European research team led by Charité—Universitätsmedizin Berlin is now aiming to revolutionize this cornerstone of the chemical industry: as part of the CarboNcare project, scientists are developing bacteria that can produce important chemical base materials from sustainable methanol—thereby replacing fossil resources.

phys-org.title: How the EU's carbon price on imports strengthens climate policies globally
phys-org.description: In early 2026, the EU extended its domestic carbon pricing to key products from beyond its borders. This is managed through the "Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism" (CBAM). Exporters of polluting goods to the EU must pay a climate tariff, unless their country has its own pricing scheme.

phys-org.title: Why the world's most ambitious coal phase‑out deal has failed, and what it means for climate finance
phys-org.description: In December 2025, Indonesia quietly abandoned plans to close the Cirebon-1 coal power plant.

phys-org.title: Roman telescope's massive infrared mirror is ready to fly
phys-org.description: NASA has completed its final inspection of the primary mirror on the Roman Space Telescope, which measures 2.4 meters (7.9 feet) in diameter and contains a layer of silver hundreds of times thinner than a human hair, at 400 nanometers.

phys-org.title: ESA selects two new scout-class missions
phys-org.description: When it comes to understanding Earth and our changing environment, space is the place. Not only does it give us an overall holistic view of the planet below, but satellite-based imagery can transcend national boundaries and give us an understanding of key changes that often go unseen at ground level.

phys-org.title: Rovers, regolith, robots: The blueprint for the moon
phys-org.description: The "soil" blanketing the moon's surface isn't actually soil. It's a fine, lethal, abrasive powder of shattered rock and jagged glass that shreds gaskets, chews through seals, and hangs in an airless environment blasted by unfiltered radiation and temperature swings that can warp steel. Scientists call it lunar regolith.

phys-org.title: Textile wastewater treatment generates alarmingly high levels of toxic compounds, study reveals
phys-org.description: Textile wastewater treatment practices inadvertently produce toxic byproducts—including chloroform and bromoform—at alarming levels that pose a clear occupational health hazard and lead to unknown environmental effects downstream, University of Massachusetts Amherst researchers have found. The study is published in the Journal of Hazardous Materials.

phys-org.title: Two decades of data show that climate change is transforming Biscayne Bay to be warmer, saltier and more acidic
phys-org.description: Climate change and sea level rise are altering the chemistry of Biscayne Bay in ways that could threaten South Florida's coastal ecosystems, water resources, fisheries, and recreation, according to a study led by scientists from the University of Miami Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science and Miami-Dade County's Department of Environmental Resources Management. Researchers found that over the past 20 years, Biscayne Bay has become warmer, saltier, and more acidic

phys-org.title: Moderate thinning increased hair lichens, while heavy cuts reduced them in Sweden
phys-org.description: By using clearcutting, industrial forestry has caused a large-scale decline of hair lichens in Sweden's forests. In a large-scale field-experiment, researchers from Umeå University, University of Northern British Columbia, Canada, and Norwegian University of Life Sciences have shown that partial cutting can increase the abundance of hair lichens. The study is published in Forest Ecology and Management.

phys-org.title: First injured Langobard woman in skeletal record reshapes view of male-only violence
phys-org.description: The Langobards are frequently depicted as fierce warrior-like people, with all known archaeological evidence of violence restricted to men. However, nearly 1,400 years ago, a Langobard woman took two severe injuries to the head, one a clean slice made by a blade, the other a crushing blow, making her the first direct evidence of interpersonal violence in Langobard females.

phys-org.title: Low-cost method uncovers conical intersections that steer light-driven molecular reactions
phys-org.description: Conical intersections are crucial molecular switching points in light-driven reactions, but accurately predicting them usually requires computations. A researcher from Shibaura Institute of Technology has developed a new low-cost quantum chemistry method that can simultaneously describe ground and excited molecular states while efficiently locating these elusive structures. The approach reproduces benchmark geometries with strong accuracy and enables practical simulations of photochemical proces

phys-org.title: Drought linked to 46% increase in sexual violence among adolescents in Southern Africa
phys-org.description: New research from the University of Oxford provides the first quantitative evidence that drought exposure over the last 12 months is associated with an increased risk of sexual, emotional and physical violence among adolescents in Southern Africa. This risk rises substantially during cumulative droughts over two years.

phys-org.title: Future jet stream changes could ease drying across Asian drylands
phys-org.description: Mid-latitude Asian drylands, stretching from Central Asia to northern China, are among the largest dryland systems in the world. Home to extensive agricultural activities and fragile ecosystems, the region is highly vulnerable to climate change and water scarcity.

phys-org.title: Bridged or not? Scientists uncover a key step in hydrogenase assembly
phys-org.description: How does nature build one of the most sophisticated catalytic metal centers found in biology? An international team of researchers has now resolved a long-standing debate surrounding the assembly of the active site of [FeFe]-hydrogenases—enzymes that rank among nature's most efficient catalysts for hydrogen production and consumption.

phys-org.title: RNA 'cut-and-patch' tool repairs faulty messages without altering DNA
phys-org.description: A research team from the School of Biomedical Sciences at the LKS Faculty of Medicine, the University of Hong Kong (HKUMed), has achieved a significant advance in biotechnology that could revolutionize treatment strategies for neurodegenerative diseases. The team has developed a novel tool called RNA Segment Editing (RSE), which functions like a "cut-and-patch" tool for RNA. This innovative approach allows scientists to precisely remove or replace faulty segments of genetic messages within livin

phys-org.title: How sargassum affects air quality, beach environments and exposure risks for families
phys-org.description: As another heavy sargassum season unfolds, many beachgoers are asking the same question: Is it safe to be near it? A recent University of Miami study offers an evidence-based answer, particularly for children. Overall risks are low, but not zero. The research, published in Exposure and Health, found that noncancer risks from arsenic exposure during beach play are minimal. But it also identified small increased cancer risks in certain scenarios, particularly from skin contact and accidental inges

phys-org.title: Living brain gene activity revealed noninvasively through programmable blood test
phys-org.description: Cell function is determined by how DNA is expressed into proteins. That process includes two main steps—transcription, when messenger RNA (mRNA) makes copies of active genes; and translation, when mRNA guides protein assembly.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.

proj-syn.title: The Tech-MAGA Breakup Is Coming
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has managed to fuse a backward-looking populist movement with a Silicon Valley vanguard whose guiding assumption is that AI will render a large share of ordinary people economically redundant. But with the tech billionaires now rewiring America's electricity grid and driving up costs, a split seems inevitable.

proj-syn.title: A Professor Should Work Hard and Grade Easy
proj-syn.description: The Harvard University faculty has now decided to limit the share of “A” grades given to students to about 20%. But, as the move's defenders freely admit, the intent is to increase professors' power and students' stress, not to generate excitement in the classroom.

proj-syn.title: What Price Hormuz?
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has three primary objectives in the Persian Gulf: unwind the Iranian nuclear program, permanently reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and not be the president blamed for having “lost” Taiwan to China. The bad news for the US president is that he can achieve at most two of these goals.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasurement of Europe’s Productivity
proj-syn.description: The Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman uses the wrong metric—purchasing power parity—to make the case that Europe is not lagging far behind the US in terms of productivity. The right metric shows that the gap is growing.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Agricultural Boom Is Faltering
proj-syn.description: The productivity growth that transformed agriculture across Latin America and the Caribbean has slowed sharply in recent years, with farmers increasingly relying on costly inputs rather than efficiency gains. Without sustained public investment, the region risks losing competitiveness and reversing decades of hard-won progress.

proj-syn.title: Americans Can’t Afford Trump’s Economy
proj-syn.description: Prices are rising faster than wages in the US, and President Donald Trump’s policies are a key reason why. Now is the time for the Democratic Party to advance a credible and specific “affordability platform” that addresses the biggest culprits, from tariffs and energy prices to mass deportation of immigrants.

proj-syn.title: Britain’s Center Cannot Hold
proj-syn.description: A combination of globalization, deindustrialization, and other forces destroyed the old model of party politics that long prevailed in developed democracies. Nowhere is this more apparent than in the United Kingdom, where voters are angry and demanding radical solutions that no political leader can actually deliver.

proj-syn.title: Reading Between China’s Red Lines
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s blunt warning to US President Donald Trump about Taiwan was clearly intended to sharpen the distinction between this ultimatum and the many others Xi has issued. But expanding the number of non-negotiable positions reduces the space for effective diplomacy and raises the risk of accidental conflict.

proj-syn.title: The Pope Should Have Gone Further on AI
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV has made waves with his first encyclical, in which he describes the development and deployment of new AI tools as a profound threat to human dignity. If anything, he has not gone far enough in pressing the question of what the technology is being designed to do.

proj-syn.title: China’s Long March to Technological Supremacy
proj-syn.description: China’s R&D prowess was visible in research output, patents, PhDs, and critical technologies for years, long before crystallizing into commercial products that Western investors, commentators, and policymakers noticed. And now it’s happening again.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s Defense of Humanity
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV is right to celebrate the grandeur of humanity, to criticize and reject posthumanism, and to emphasize the essential, categorical, and insurmountable difference between humans and machines. His first encyclical is a necessary exhortation to believers and non-believers alike.
